title: HYPOChLorous Acid TEsting Studies: ELECTIVE Surgeries
summary: Hypoclates:Elective investigates which irrigation solution used during planned (elective) visceral surgical procedures of the abdomen, thorax, and pelvis is best suited to prevent surgical site infections (SSI). Operations in these regions inherently carry a relevant risk of wound infections, which can lead to prolonged hospital stays, additional interventions, and an increased burden on patients. This study compares two different irrigation strategies: the previous standard method using isotonic saline (single intraoperative irrigation) and a single intraoperative irrigation with 3 liters of Granudacyn® – a medical device containing hypochlorous acid (HOCl), which is already used in wound care, particularly for deep, infected, or chronic wounds. The main objective is to determine which irrigation method is more effective in reducing wound infections after elective operations. The results of this study may help to adapt future treatment recommendations for elective visceral surgical procedures and thereby improve clinical outcomes and recovery for patients. In addition, Hypoclates:Elective is among the first studies to investigate the potential beneficial effect of HOCl in surgical site infection prophylaxis across a large patient population.
conditions: Infection following a procedure, not elsewhere classified
